 30 Minute Lightning Lesson: From Search to Shelf (Call Numbers)
 In-Person
 What happens after you find a book in the library catalog? How do you navigate the library stacks? 
 Join this short 30 minute lesson to learn how library call numbers are organized and how to use them to efficiently find books and other materials on the shelves. This interactive session will guide you through short activities to better understand the Library of Congress classification system and build confidence navigating the library collection. The Library of Congress (LC) classification system is an alphanumeric system used primarily by academic and research libraries to organize books. 
 NYU Libraries is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. If you have an accommodation request, please email lib-reference@nyu.edu . Additionally, masks are always welcome on NYU's campuses and facilities.
